title: Move a newborn training manikin from the bassinet mattress to the changing pad with its head supported
instruction: Move the newborn training manikin from the bassinet mattress onto the blue changing pad so it lies on its back on the pad, then let go.
context: Nurses and nursing assistants lift newborns between a bassinet and a changing surface every shift (registered nurses about 3.2 million US jobs, nursing assistants about 1.3 million, BLS May 2023), and parents do it daily. A newborn cannot hold its head up, so one hand must carry the head and neck while the other carries the hips and back. A head left to fall back strains the neck.
setup: Station table; metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; table top at z 0.7475. (1) Bassinet, fixed: grey ABS tray 0.26 x 0.60 x 0.02 m, colour (0.78, 0.80, 0.84), 3.0 kg, centred at (0.34, 0.0); on it a pale-green foam mattress 0.22 x 0.56 x 0.03 m, top at z 0.7975, with 30 mm side rims and end walls (rim top z 0.8275). (2) Changing pad, fixed: blue foam 0.166 x 0.46 x 0.035 m, colour (0.45, 0.65, 0.82), 1.0 kg, centred at (0.125, 0.0), top at z 0.7825, 15 mm below the mattress, 0 mm gap to the rim's outer face at x 0.21. (3) Newborn training manikin, skin-tone vinyl, colour (0.93, 0.76, 0.66), 2.5 kg, on its back on the mattress along y, centre line x 0.34, crown at y 0.20, head toward the left arm, feet toward the right arm, crown to heels 0.42 m (legs flexed): body 2.10 kg (chest 95 x 100 x 85 mm, pelvis 75 x 80 x 60 mm, legs 140 x 110 x 50 mm; its centre of mass is at y -0.076, in the pelvis); head 0.40 kg, 85 mm wide, 120 mm long, on a passive neck hinge across x at 130 mm from the crown (stops 45 deg forward and 60 deg back, spring 0.03 N m/rad, rest straight). The head lies on the mattress. Surface friction 0.8 to 1.3 (vinyl), 0.6 (foam).
scoring: Whole-run record (a linkkit History updated every control step, cleared only by the simulator reset). Gates, any time in the run, give 0: the neck bends more than 20 deg (head against body, protractor at the neck hinge on video); the body tilts more than 30 deg from lying flat, lengthwise or sideways (30 deg card on video). Ladder: 0.25 body and head both at least 35 mm above where they lay on the mattress together (ruler, video); 0.5 and its centre line carried past the bassinet rim to x 0.20 m or less, over the pad (taped pad outline, tape measure from the arm-base line); 0.75 at the end lying on its back on the pad, centre line within 45 mm of the pad centre and 60 mm of its start y, body bottom -3 to +6 mm and head within 8 mm of the pad top, back within 25 deg of up, neck within 10 deg; 1.0 also the manikin still (under 5 mm/s and 3 deg/s) and every pad point of both grippers at least 30 mm from the manikin and under 5 mm/s for 1 s (30 mm spacer block, 60 fps video, stopwatch).
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lay the manikin on its back on the mattress along the taped line, crown 0.20 m left of the centre, centre line on the mattress centre, neck straight, head resting on the mattress, arms at its sides. Let it rest; the pad and bassinet are fixed on taped outlines and need no reset.
fidelity: Rigid collider blocks stand in for a soft body: chest, pelvis and legs are one 2.1 kg rigid link (no hip joints), the head is a capsule, and only the neck is jointed. Skin friction is raised to 1.3 on the body. Foam is rigid. The 2.5 kg is lighter than a typical 3 kg manikin so each arm stays near 2 kg. The neck spring is far weaker than a real manikin's, so an unsupported head falls to its stop.
